subject: Civic Education
sourceFile: Copy of National Value Education BECE Syllabus - syllabusNG (1).txt
examFormat: National Values Education (NVE) is a fusion of Civic Education, Security Education and Social Studies; it assesses the development of Nigerian youth as responsible citizens, their moral, social, political and intellectual knowledge in nation-building, their ability to recognise the dimensions of human beings in different cultural and social contexts, and their level of security consciousness. Civic Education is examined in Paper 1 of BECE National Values Education, which has sixty multiple-choice questions: 50 from Civic Education and 10 from Security Education. (Social Studies is examined separately in Paper 2.)
excluded: Left out the syllabus.ng "About Us", "About BECE", eligibility, grading, registration, table of contents and FAQ chapters (publisher marketing / general information, not syllabus content). Security Education and Social Studies themes are in their own files. The truncated sixth Democracy topic heading ("Democratic …") was named "Democratic Voting" from its content.

Civic Education for Junior Secondary Schools — Mencke O. et al. (Serolak Concepts)

Pacific Education for Upper UBE Classes with Work Book for JSS 1–3 — G. E. Ikwueze et al. (Pacific Publishers)
Current Civic Education for JSS 1–3 — Jibike V. U. et al. (MIS.FAV Publishers)
Comprehensive Studies on National Values for Junior Secondary School: Civic Education, Social Studies and Security Education — Meneka, Obiageli Augustina (Direct View Media)

topics.name: National Values: Honesty, Cooperation and Self-Reliance
objectives: Explain the meaning, levels of manifestation and importance of values in the society
Explain the meaning, attributes and benefits of honesty and the consequences of dishonesty
Explain the meaning, attributes, promoting factors and benefits of cooperation
Explain the meaning, attributes and benefits of self-reliance
topics.content: Sub-theme: Our Values. Covers values, honesty, cooperation and self-reliance as national values.

subtopics.name: Values
objectives: Explain the meaning of values: likes and dislikes
Identify the levels of manifestation of values: individual and society
State the importance of values in the society: unity, cooperation and harmony
Identify factors that promote a value system: consistency, trust, tolerance, fairness, integrity and commitment

subtopics.name: Honesty
objectives: Explain the meaning of honesty
List the attributes of honesty
State the benefits of honesty
Explain the consequences of dishonesty, e.g. in examination malpractice, cheating and fraudulent practices

subtopics.name: Cooperation
objectives: Explain the meaning of cooperation
List the attributes of cooperation: sharing, caring, supporting etc.
Identify factors that promote cooperation
State the benefits of cooperation: harmony, progress and goal achievement

subtopics.name: Self-Reliance
objectives: Explain the meaning of self-reliance
List the attributes of self-reliance
Describe the processes of identifying, nurturing and perfecting talents and skills
State the benefits of self-reliance to oneself, the family and the society
Understand that the wealth of a nation is contained in its natural and human resources
Explain the consequences of undiscovered talents and undeveloped skills

topics.name: National Values: Integrity, Contentment, Discipline and Courage
objectives: Explain the meaning and attributes of integrity, contentment, discipline and courage
topics.content: Sub-theme: Our Values. The syllabus heading names integrity, contentment and discipline; courage is listed under the same topic.

subtopics.name: Integrity
objectives: Explain the meaning of integrity
List the attributes of integrity: probity and honesty, contentment, truthfulness, fair-play and non-compromise of principles
Give examples of people of integrity in the society
Explain the need for people of integrity in the society

subtopics.name: Contentment
objectives: Explain the meaning of contentment
List the attributes of contentment: satisfaction, lack of envy, rejection of greed and corruption, humility etc.
Explain the effects of lack of contentment on the society: corruption, greed, envy, prostitution, robbery, cheating etc.

subtopics.name: Discipline
objectives: Explain the meaning of discipline
List the attributes of discipline: self-control, moderation, modesty, respect for legitimate authority, respect for rules and regulations, perseverance, dedication etc.

subtopics.name: Courage
objectives: Explain the meaning of courage
Identify the types of courage: physical, moral and spiritual
List the attributes of a courageous person: commitment, endurance, determination, steadfastness, diligence, boldness, bravery etc.

topics.name: National Values: Right Attitude to Work
objectives: Explain the meaning of right attitude to work
List the attributes of right attitude to work: honesty, discipline, integrity, commitment, punctuality, regularity, consistency, diligence, transparency etc.
State the importance of reward: higher productivity, efficiency, progress, recognition and improved national image
Explain the consequences of not having the right attitude to work: declining productivity, lack of motivation, indiscipline and national disasters (air, sea, road etc.)

topics.name: Negative Behaviour
objectives: Explain the meaning of negative behaviour
Identify types of negative behaviour: dishonesty, excessive love of money, ostentatious living, disregard for time, drug trafficking, examination malpractice, cultism etc.
Explain the effects of negative behaviour: value disorientation, inefficiency, high crime rate etc.
Suggest ways of promoting positive behaviour

topics.name: Citizenship
objectives: Explain the meaning of citizenship
Identify the types of citizenship: by birth, by registration and by naturalisation
Describe the process of becoming a citizen of a country

topics.name: Rights and Duties of a Citizen
objectives: Explain the meaning of rights and duties
Differentiate between rights and duties
State the importance of citizens' rights and duties: social control, peace, due process and discipline

topics.name: Supremacy of the Constitution
objectives: Explain the supremacy of the constitution

topics.name: The Constitution
objectives: Explain the meaning of constitution
Identify the constitutions of colonial Nigeria: Clifford Constitution 1922, Richards Constitution 1946, Macpherson Constitution 1951, Lyttelton Constitution 1954 and Independence Constitution 1960
State the features of the colonial constitutions
Identify the post-1960 constitutions: 1963, 1979 and 1989 Constitutions
State the features of the post-1960 constitutions

topics.name: Objects for National Consciousness
objectives: Identify the national symbols: coat of arms, national flag and national currency
Recite and explain the National Anthem and Pledge
State the purpose of establishing national institutions like the NYSC, Unity Schools and Federal Character
Suggest ways of promoting national unity: tolerance, hospitality, non-discrimination, inter-marriage etc.

topics.name: Nigeria as a Federation
objectives: Explain the meaning of federation
State the need for federation: national integration, unity in diversity and controlling activities of states

Describe the characteristics of a federation: sharing of powers between central and state governments; states have constitutionally defined control over their own affairs; central government controls the states; constitution of the federation

topics.name: Relationship Between Federal, State and Local Governments
objectives: Describe the relationship between the tiers of government: performing functions according to constitutional provisions, power to legislate, and power to carry out functions in accordance with constitutional provisions
Differentiate among the three tiers of government in functions, legislative powers, executive powers, and concurrent and exclusive powers

topics.name: The Rule of Law
objectives: Explain the meaning of law and rule of law
State the benefits of rule of law as against arbitrary rule
Explain punishment for breaking the law
Explain the equality of all citizens before the law
topics.content: Sub-theme: Human Rights and the Rule of Law.

topics.name: Protection of Human Rights and the Rule of Law
objectives: Describe ways of protecting human rights: representing the affected persons in court; drawing attention to cases of human rights violations through protest marches, media coverage and hunger strikes
Identify groups that assist in protecting the human rights of citizens: civil society organisations (e.g. CLO, CDHR, CRP), trade unions, students unions, ethnic associations and the Legal Aid Council
topics.content: Sub-theme: Human Rights and the Rule of Law.

topics.name: Consumer Rights and Responsibilities
objectives: State the universal rights of a consumer: satisfaction of basic needs, safety, information, redress, consumer education, representation (to be heard) and a healthy environment
State the responsibilities of a consumer: be aware, demand and keep proofs of transactions (receipts, invoices, warranties etc.), think independently, speak out and respect the environment
topics.content: Sub-theme: Human Rights and the Rule of Law.

topics.name: Democracy
objectives: Explain the meaning of democracy
State the features of democracy
Identify democratic institutions and their functions: INEC, political parties, pressure groups and arms of government
State the importance of democracy

topics.name: Pillars of Democracy
objectives: Explain the meaning of pillars of democracy
Identify the pillars of democracy: the people, democratic institutions, rule of law, transparent electoral process, majority rule and minority rights etc.

topics.name: Election and Voter Responsibilities
objectives: Explain the concepts of election, voter and voting
Differentiate between various types of elections
Enumerate the basic qualifications for election
Discuss the responsibilities of a voter
Describe the procedure for voting and discuss the importance of election

topics.name: Electoral Malpractices
objectives: Explain the meaning of electoral malpractice

Identify forms of electoral malpractice: fake ballot papers, manipulation of votes and multiple voting; artificial scarcity of electoral materials; underage voting; thuggery and intimidation; inducement and corruption; fake manifestoes

topics.name: Elections and Electoral Bodies in Nigeria
objectives: Explain the meaning and importance of elections
Identify the electoral bodies: INEC and SIEC for national and state government respectively
Explain the need for free and fair elections
Identify electoral malpractices in Nigeria and how to prevent them

topics.name: Democratic Voting
objectives: Explain the meaning of voting
Describe voters registration
State the importance of voting
Describe the process of voting
topics.content: Sub-theme: Democracy. (The topic heading is cut off in the source text after "Democratic"; its content is about voting.)
